_doc: Rival clans: how their feelings toward us change, when they raid, trade and send messengers, how strong their people are, and how their chiefs weigh a deal. Times in days unless named *_s. Texts are English translation keys; [key, var...] texts take the clan's values (clan_name, chief, n...). See docs/CONFIG.md. The checks on LLM parley output (rivals.sanitize_terms/check_reply) stay in code.

ledger._doc: What passed between us and each clan, dated (rivals.note; make_it_fun C1): our deeds to them (the deeds above, their reason as the words) and these kinds: text in the chief's words (vars in order), weight (+ good for us, - bad). The chief brings up the weightiest (|weight| at least quote_min, fading with age: half its pull after half_days days) in dilemmas with the clan and when the offline chief answers an envoy: quote (when, text) and a closing remark from tags (bad/good; _inherited for what happened under the chief before, %s = that chief). keep: entries kept per clan. dates: how a date is said (%s = the season).

chiefs._doc: Rival chiefs as people (rivals.gd; make_it_fun C1). A chief rules reign_days (a range), then dies and a successor takes the seat (rivals.succeed, also a game master's verb): a name and epithet from names for the clan's culture, another temper, and the relation drawn reset of the way to the clan's base + the new temper's base. The ledger stays: the successor inherits it. tempers: word (how the chronicle names it), base (added to the relation the clan drifts to), hostility (raid hostility mult), deal (added to how good a parley deal looks to them). first: the first chief's temper by culture. log: the succession (old chief, clan, new chief, epithet, temper word).
chiefs.log: %s, chief of the %s, has died. %s %s leads them now: %s.

nemesis._doc: One horizon threat at a time (rivals.gd; make_it_fun C2). The nemesis is picked once: at a first contact the clan met takes the part if its score (minus its relation, + pick.martial for a martial clan) is at least pick.min_score; if none has by pick.by_day, the worst of the clans met (not allies or vassals). A game master may set it (rivals.set_nemesis). While the feud runs the nemesis raids and demands from hostile_at (other clans from raids.hostile_at), its raid timer is raid_every_mult as long, the other clans' others_every_mult (they fall back, not silent), and the stage for the tribe's era (stages: the last whose era has come) adds warriors to each raid band, multiplies its demands and shortens its raid timer. The feud ends when the nemesis is in one of over_stances, at peace, our vassal, or beaten at home over_defeats times; holding off its first raid and the end of the feud are achievements (feats, %s = the clan). marked: what the tribe is told when the nemesis is chosen (clan vars).
